name: RSP Western States Heritage Championship
epitaph: The promotion's own main championship, first won in a triple threat that closed its debut pay-per-view after an eight-man battle royal and a sudden-death match narrowed the field. Its first two reigns both ended at the same event, the promotion's own Dangerous Games, the first inside the ring and the second outside every document the newsgroup itself preserves.

name: RSP Television Championship
epitaph: Named for whichever sponsor could afford the promotion's own public-access airtime in a given week, the belt was first won in a four-corners match and changed hands at the same Dangerous Games pay-per-view that turned over the promotion's own top title.

name: RSP Tag Team Championship
epitaph: First won by a beatdown finish the broadcast's own commentary called into question, the belts were held up entirely by the promotion's own vice president after a three-way defense at Dangerous Games ended too confused to call.

name: RSP Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Handed to its first champion outright by promotion president Sean Christopher rather than contested for, the title changed hands within weeks to a wrestler who insists to this day that his own shoulders were never pinned.
